column1: # The model registry — pipe-separated, one row per servable model.
# NAME    the directory under models/ holding the weights, and the name every surface uses
# REPO    HuggingFace MLX repo the weights came from (provenance; nothing here ever pulls)
# DRAFT   MTP draft repo for speculative decoding, or "-" for none
# PORT    default server port — distinct per model so several could run side by side. 8080 is
#         deliberately unused: Docker Desktop binds it (http-alt) for as long as it runs, so a row
#         claiming it fails PortUnavailable on any machine with Docker up.
# SIZE    upstream weight size in GB (du reports GiB, so it reads ~7% smaller)
# FLAGS   this model's best-quality serving flags, space-separated, or "-"
# PARAMS  request-body fields sent with every generation as key=value, space-separated, or "-".
#         Values are JSON, so enable_thinking=false is the boolean and not the string. Separate
#         from FLAGS because a chat template that defaults a behaviour ON cannot be talked out of
#         it by a server flag: the flag's absence leaves the template variable UNDEFINED, which is
#         not false. The request body is the only lever that reaches such a template.
# NOTE    what this one is for, and measured behaviour worth not re-deriving
# A row is a claim about what is available UPSTREAM; only the store proves what is on disk.
# Adding a row does not pull anything — downloads stay explicit and user-initiated.
# NOTE must not contain "|": rows are split positionally and a stray pipe is refused by name.
NAME|REPO|DRAFT|PORT|SIZE|FLAGS|PARAMS|NOTE

Gemma4-26B-A4B|lmstudio-community/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-MLX-6bit|-|8083|21.8G|--enable-thinking|-|MoE, ~4B active/token: 61 tok/s decode, 2070 tok/s prefill - 5x the rest on both. Vision + audio, 262K ctx.

Qwen3.8-27B|lmstudio-community/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-6bit|lukaskremla/Qwen3.8-27B-MTP-6bit-MLX|8089|22.8G|--enable-thinking|enable_thinking=false|Reasoning + agentic coding flagship. Dense, so 24 tok/s with MTP and 427 tok/s prefill; 12.5 tok/s measured here without the draft. Vision, 262K ctx. The MTP draft weights are NOT in the store - pull them before relying on speculative decoding. Thinking is switched off in the REQUEST, never by dropping the server flag: with no preference expressed the template variable is left undefined and Qwen3.8's own template reads undefined as on, so thinking survives the flag's absence. It has to be off because thinking-mode output arrives UNFENCED and the edit applier needs a fenced whole-file block - measured 342 reasoning chars and bare code with the field omitted, 0 and fenced code with it false, and 0 of 7 benchmark cases scored before it was set.

Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated|ailexleon/Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated-mlx-6Bit|-|8081|22.8G|--enable-thinking|enable_thinking=false|Huihui abliteration of the above - refusal directions removed. No MTP draft, so 12 tok/s. Vision, 262K ctx. Same chat template as the row above, so it needs the same in-request thinking switch for the same reason.

Gemma4-31B|lmstudio-community/gemma-4-31B-it-MLX-6bit|-|8082|26.1G|--enable-thinking --kv-bits 8 --quantized-kv-start 8192|-|Google dense generalist, the slowest here at 7 tok/s. 140+ languages, strong math. 8-bit KV: fp16 needs 43.8G at 262K and will not fit.

Qwen3-Coder-30B|lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-MLX-6bit|-|8084|24.8G|-|-|MoE, 3.3B active/token so fast decode like Gemma-MoE. Instruct (no thinking channel). Qwen3-Coder flagship coder, 256K ctx.

GLM-4.7-Flash|lmstudio-community/GLM-4.7-Flash-MLX-6bit|-|8085|24.0G|-|-|MoE ~30B, Zhipu GLM coder-generalist. Instruct. Measured 38.1 tok/s decode, and 2 of 7 benchmark cases - the lowest scorer that still produced code, with two cases emitting Python that does not parse at all.

Qwen3-Coder-Next-4bit|lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit|-|8087|44.9G|-|-|4bit, so it breaks the 6bit parity of the rest - a win despite lower fidelity is strong, a loss is confounded. qwen3_next hybrid MoE, 80B total / ~3B active (10 of 512 experts) so fast decode. Served and benchmarked end to end on mlx-vlm 0.6.17 at ~46 tok/s decode, loading in under 2 min; it fits 64G alongside a normal desktop, at 19% free memory. 256K ctx.

Muse-Glimmer-30B-6bit|mlx-community/Muse-Glimmer-30B-6bit|-|8086|26.4G|-|-|DENSE 30B, and it decodes like one: 11.5 tok/s, near Gemma4-31B rather than the MoE coders. muse_glimmer vision-language architecture, present in mlx-vlm 0.6.17's model set (checked against the installed package, not assumed). 52 layers, GQA with 2 KV heads, 2048 sliding window, silu, logit softcapping. Instruct, and the config ships do_sample false. 128K ctx. Scores 7 of 7 benchmark cases - the slowest perfect scorer at 38 min, and the untidiest at 49 style findings. This row previously called the model UNUSABLE on the strength of 1 content token in 338s and a bare probe returning 0 in 180s, and blamed harmony-style channel markup; that was the loop misreading a cold weight load as a hang, not the model or its channels, and the reading did not survive the guard being fixed.

gpt-oss-20b|mlx-community/gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8|-|8088|12.1G|-|-|OpenAI open-weight, the smallest and fastest to load here. gpt_oss MoE 20.9B total / ~3.6B active (4 of 32 experts). NATIVE MXFP4 (4bit experts + 8bit attn = the Q8) - the reference build, not a downgrade, but a distinct quant tier from the 6bit rows. REASONING model: harmony format plus a reasoning_effort/analysis channel, so probe whether reasoning_content arrives separate (clean) or inline (derails) before trusting the non-thinking driver. 128K ctx.
